sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. Change Request 2019-002 and New Code Request [hng] Hungu (submitted by Linda Jordan, SIL International / Instituto de Linguas Nacionais Angola, 2018-08-31; adopted 2020-01-23).
sources.note: Nothing on stress/tone. Sociolinguistic rationale only: 2014/2017 wordlists (two Hungu varieties, Uige and Bengo, 80% shared; 62-69% with Nsoso and Mphombo Kikongo; 47-55% with Kimbundu Ngaji/Ngongembo), dialect-mapping; autonym Kihungu, exonym Dihungu; ~500,000 speakers. Cites Jordan 2017 unpublished survey report.

sources.citation: de Schryver, Gilles-Maurice, Rebecca Grollemund, Simon Branford & Koen Bostoen. 2015. Introducing a state-of-the-art phylogenetic classification of the Kikongo Language Cluster. Africana Linguistica 21: 87-162.
sources.note: Open on Persee but bot-could not be reached by automated download; documents exactly which sources/fieldwork underlie 'Hungu' and 'Pombo' in the KLC and their South Kikongo placement (identity check for hung1280), though no stress statement is expected.

sources.citation: Atkins, Guy. 1955. A demographic survey of the Kimbundu-Kongo language border in Angola. Boletim da Sociedade de Geografia de Lisboa, ser. 73, n. 7-9: 325-347. (archive.org DLI item dli.ernet.535727, whole issue)
sources.note: Nothing on Hungu stress or tone. Atkins says Hungu (S.E. Kongo dialect, ~60,000 speakers, sub-dialects Mafundi, Ngumbi, Nguenza, Tsotso of Puri) 'has been described in a separate paper' (the 1954 Garcia de Orta outline, footnote p. 327) and gives only demographic/dialect-boundary notes. The article's only prosodic remark concerns Holu (Holo, H33-adjacent but a different language): 'Phonology: Holu has a distinction of length in radical vowels, but no radical stress' (p. 345).

sources.note: The only published grammatical description of Hungu (H33); cited by Herbert 1986 for its phonology (prenasalization) and used by BantUGent as the sole Dihungu data source; written by a Bantu tonologist, so it very likely states whether Hungu has tone and/or radical/penultimate stress.
